title: AGL Securities Dealing Policy
date_next_review: Biennial review by AGL's Audit and Risk Management Committee, with changes approved by the AGL Board; no fixed date stated

tiers.name: AGL Employees
tiers.description: Each director, officer and employee of the Group, and each contractor and consultant to the Group who are contractually bound to comply with the Policy. All of the substantive prohibitions (blackout periods, short-term dealing, short selling, stock lending, unvested derivatives, margin loans and other secured financing) apply at this level.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: An AGL Employee who is an AGL Director, a member of AGL's Executive Team, a member of AGL's Enterprise Leadership Team, an executive assistant of an Executive Team member, or is designated as such by the Company Secretary from time to time. Must obtain written approval before any dealing in AGL Securities at any time, expressly including dealings in Derivatives over fully vested AGL Shares.

tiers.name: AGL Directors
tiers.description: Directors of AGL. Designated Persons whose dealings are approved by the Chair of the AGL Board (or the Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chair's own dealing), and who must notify the Company Secretary of dealings for ASX Appendix 3Y purposes.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: In relation to a Designated Person: close family members including a spouse or partner and dependent children, and companies, partnerships, trusts and other entities (such as family trusts or self-managed superannuation funds) controlled by the Designated Person or any close family member. The Policy is read as if references to Designated Person were references to Connected Persons.

definitions.hedging_definition: any other arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in AGL Securities or which itself or in combination with one or more other Derivatives would have the effect of providing an AGL Employee with a greater benefit than would otherwise have been realised in respect of the unvested AGL Securities

windows.end_anchor: close of business on the day after AGL announces its preliminary final results (Appendix 4E)
close of business on the day after AGL announces its half year results (Appendix 4D)

windows.start_anchor: immediately following the end of each blackout period
windows.end_anchor: four weeks after the end of that blackout period

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time. These are confidential: to protect confidentiality there may not be any internal notification that a prohibition on dealing is in place, and the Company Secretary may advise that a prohibition exists when an approval request is received but may not be in a position to explain why or how long it will be in place.

rules.detail: Flat prohibition on using Derivatives in relation to any unvested AGL Securities, on the stated rationale that they would allow value to be realised even if performance hurdles are not met. Derivatives takes its section 761D meaning and expressly extends to any arrangement that limits the economic risk of an unvested holding.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested AGL Securities.

rules.detail: The permission for Derivatives over vested AGL Securities is conditional on the Securities not being subject to a holding lock, so vested but holding-locked shares (for example under AGL's Employee Share Plan) cannot be collared.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided any dealing in those Derivatives complies with the other requirements of this Policy (including approval requirements) and the AGL Securities are not subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested, unlocked AGL Securities are expressly permitted subject to the Policy's approval requirements, and paragraph 4.2 puts the point beyond doubt for Designated Persons. Securities includes Derivatives as defined in section 761D and financial products under section 1042A with no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call with a bank is within scope. Approval is discretionary, withdrawable without reason and valid for one week.
rules.evidence: For the avoidance of doubt, this requirement includes any proposed dealing in Derivatives in respect of fully vested AGL Shares.

rules.detail: Exchange traded options and warrants are expressly identified as Securities in the Purpose section, and are treated no differently from OTC derivatives: prior written approval, outside blackout periods, no inside information, no holding lock and compliance with the short-term dealing ban.
rules.evidence: The definition of Securities is complex but includes shares in a company and derivative instruments such as exchange traded options and warrants.

rules.detail: An AGL Employee who is not a Designated Person needs no approval to deal in Derivatives over vested, unlocked AGL Securities, but must still stay outside blackout periods, hold no inside information, satisfy the Front Page Test and comply with the short-term dealing, short selling and secured financing prohibitions.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided any dealing in those Derivatives complies with the other requirements of this Policy

rules.detail: Hedging of unvested holdings is caught both by the ban on Derivatives over unvested AGL Securities and by the anti-avoidance limb of the Derivatives definition, which sweeps in any other arrangement operating to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding or that in combination would confer a greater benefit than would otherwise have been realised.
rules.evidence: any other arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in AGL Securities

rules.detail: Vested AGL Securities subject to a holding lock fall outside the permission in 3.6 and so cannot be hedged with Derivatives; the exceptional circumstances route in 5.1 is also expressly unavailable for Securities subject to a restriction on disposal.
rules.evidence: the AGL Securities are not subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Hedging vested, unlocked AGL Securities with Derivatives is expressly permitted for Designated Persons with prior written approval from the person set out in the 4.2 matrix, executed within the one week approval validity and outside blackout periods.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided any dealing in those Derivatives complies with the other requirements of this Policy (including approval requirements)

rules.detail: Non-Designated employees may hedge vested, unlocked holdings without approval, subject to the blackout periods, insider trading rules, Front Page Test and the 3.4 short-term dealing ban.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is a dealing because it acquires or disposes of an economic interest and involves granting a right or obligation to dispose of Securities, so it requires prior written approval. Any monetisation funded by a loan for which AGL Securities may be used as security is separately prohibited by 3.7.
rules.evidence: granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising, or discharging an option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of the Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short selling for all AGL Employees, described as borrowing a security and selling it in the hope of buying it back at a lower price to close out the short position.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into short selling or stock lending arrangements in relation to AGL Securities.

rules.detail: Stock lending arrangements in relation to AGL Securities are banned outright for all AGL Employees, with no approval route. This removes the ability to lend the collared shares to the bank or to support any borrow-based structure.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into short selling or stock lending arrangements in relation to AGL Securities.

rules.detail: CFDs are not named but are Derivatives within section 761D and so Securities. Over vested unlocked shares a Designated Person would need prior written approval, but in practice a CFD would be difficult to reconcile with the ban on dealing as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis, and a short CFD would engage the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees must not deal in AGL Securities as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis.

rules.detail: A CFD referencing unvested AGL Securities is a Derivative in relation to unvested AGL Securities and so within the flat 3.6 prohibition.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested AGL Securities.

rules.detail: Margin loan arrangements are prohibited for every AGL Employee, both where they fund the acquisition of AGL Securities and where AGL Securities may be used as security against repayment. There is no approval, exceptional circumstances or grandfathering carve-out. Arrangements such as margin loans that could result in disposal within 3 months of acquisition are separately banned by 3.4.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements (and other secured financing arrangements) to fund the acquisition of AGL Securities or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

rules.detail: Granting security is not itself defined as a dealing, but 3.7 prohibits any arrangement in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as security against repayment of a loan. The prohibition is drafted at the level of possible use as security, so even a facility under which the shares merely may be charged is caught. An encumbrance unconnected with any loan is not addressed.
rules.evidence: or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

rules.detail: The ban extends beyond margin loans to 'other secured financing arrangements', applies to all AGL Employees and their Connected Persons where practicable, and is not limited by vesting state, tier or amount. No approver is given power to waive it and the exceptional circumstances regime in 5.1 addresses only disposals during blackout periods.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements (and other secured financing arrangements) to fund the acquisition of AGL Securities or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

rules.detail: Two limbs: a general ban on dealing as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis, and a hard 3 month holding period from acquisition that also catches entering into arrangements (margin loans are the stated example) which could result in the Securities being disposed of within 3 months. Carve-outs for securities from options or rights held at least 3 months, shares acquired under an AGL employee equity plan, and share rights under a pro rata entitlement offer.
rules.evidence: AGL Employees who acquire AGL Securities must not dispose of those Securities, or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those Securities being disposed of, within 3 months of acquisition.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary for all other Designated Persons; CEO for Executive Team members and the Company Secretary; Chair of the AGL Board for non-executive Directors, the CEO and the CFO; Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for the Chair of the AGL Board; a nominated alternate if the approver is unavailable
clearance.evidence: Any approval to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused by the applicable approver in his or her absolute discretion without giving reason. ... Any approval to undertake the proposed dealing will be valid for one week unless it is withdrawn.

clearance.approver: Chair of the AGL Board (Chair of the Audit & Risk Management Committee for a dealing by the Chair of the AGL Board)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (who lodges Appendix 3Y with the ASX)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as practicable and in any case no later than close of business on the second day after the dealing is entered into
clearance.evidence: AGL Directors must notify the Company Secretary as soon as practicable (and, in any case, no later than close of business on the second day after the dealing is entered into).

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (or, for a Designated Person, the approver specified in paragraph 4.2 or their nominated alternate). Required only for a disposal during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances; no routine clearance applies to non-Designated employees.
clearance.evidence: In addition, all AGL Employees (not just Designated Persons) must seek approval to deal in AGL Securities during a blackout period (i.e. due to exceptional circumstances).

clearance.approver: The approver applicable to the associated Designated Person under the paragraph 4.2 matrix
clearance.evidence: a Designated Person must take appropriate steps for Connected Persons to ... seek approval for any proposed dealings in AGL Securities

short_term.basis: from acquisition; also catches entering into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in disposal within that period
carve_outs: Securities acquired as a result of the exercise of an option or similar right where the option or right has been held for at least 3 months
AGL shares acquired under an AGL employee equity plan, including AGL's Long Term Incentive Plan, AGL's Share Purchase Plan, or AGL's Employee Share Reward Plan
Share rights acquired pursuant to an entitlement offer made on a pro rata basis to AGL Shareholders
short_term.evidence: AGL Employees must not deal in AGL Securities as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis.

exceptions.evidence: the acquisition of AGL Securities under an AGL employee equity plan, including AGL's Long Term Incentive Plan, AGL's Employee Share Plan or AGL's Share Purchase Plan
the acquisition of AGL Securities under AGL's Dividend Reinvestment Plan

the acquisition of AGL Securities as a result of the exercise of rights acquired pursuant to an entitlement offer made on a pro rata basis to all AGL Shareholders; the on-market sale of rights acquired pursuant to an entitlement offer
the disposal of AGL Securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back

dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the AGL Securities (for example, transfers of AGL Securities already held by a Designated Person into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Designated Person is a beneficiary)

trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the AGL Employee or Connected Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the AGL Employee or Connected Person to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period

exceptions.approver: The approver specified in paragraph 4.2 (or their nominated alternate) for Designated Persons, otherwise the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: the AGL Employee is experiencing severe financial hardship and can only meet their financial commitments by selling their Securities

exceptions.approver: The approver specified in paragraph 4.2 (or their nominated alternate) for Designated Persons, otherwise the Company Secretary
exceptions.evidence: compulsion by court order or there are other exceptional circumstances

external_documents: AGL Long Term Incentive Plan rules
AGL Employee Share Reward Plan / Employee Share Plan rules
exemption_authority: Paragraph 5.1 only, and only for disposals: the paragraph 4.2 approver (or nominated alternate) for Designated Persons, otherwise the Company Secretary, may approve a disposal during a blackout period where the employee is in severe financial hardship and can only meet financial commitments by selling, is compelled by court order, or there are other exceptional circumstances, provided they hold no inside information, the Securities are not subject to a restriction on disposal, and the application is supported by sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action. The Company Secretary keeps a record and must promptly inform the Board. No authority exists to waive the paragraph 3.7 margin loan and secured financing prohibition, the 3.5 short selling and stock lending bans, or the 3.6 unvested derivatives ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements (and other secured financing arrangements) to fund the acquisition of AGL Securities or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is a secured financing arrangement in relation to which AGL Securities would be used as security against repayment, so it is prohibited outright for every AGL Employee with no approval route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The trigger is the possibility of the shares being used as security, not actual granting of the charge, so even a negative pledge structure or a facility with an optional security mechanic over AGL shares is caught.

bespoke_clauses.topic: derivatives over vested shares expressly allowed
bespoke_clauses.clause: For the avoidance of doubt, this requirement includes any proposed dealing in Derivatives in respect of fully vested AGL Shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The unfunded legs of a collar over fully vested, unlocked shares are contemplated and approvable, so the structure fails only on the financing leg; a cash-settled or unfunded collar could still be presented for approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives ... includes options, forward contracts, swaps, futures contracts and warrants and any combination of one or more of these things or any other arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in AGL Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A synthetic or combination structure over unvested entitlements cannot be engineered around the 3.6 ban, since the definition is drafted by economic effect rather than instrument type.

bespoke_clauses.clause: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided ... the AGL Securities are not subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank must verify not only vesting but the absence of any holding lock on the specific parcel before the collar legs may be written.

bespoke_clauses.clause: AGL Employees who acquire AGL Securities must not dispose of those Securities, or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those Securities being disposed of, within 3 months of acquisition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Independently of 3.7, a collar with physical settlement or lender enforcement rights over recently acquired shares is an arrangement that could result in disposal within 3 months, so tenor and share selection matter.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where the Board imposes additional blackout periods from time to time, to protect confidentiality there may not be any internal notification by AGL that a prohibition on dealing is in place.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undisclosed blackouts can block entry, roll or unwind at any time, and the executive may only learn of one when an approval request is refused without explanation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval to trade can be given, withdrawn, or refused by the applicable approver in his or her absolute discretion without giving reason. ... Any approval to undertake the proposed dealing will be valid for one week unless it is withdrawn.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the derivative legs is revocable up to execution and lapses after one week, so pricing must be completed inside a short window and the bank carries the risk of late withdrawal.

bespoke_clauses.clause: There are certain times during the year when approval under this Policy is more likely to be granted. These are the four-week periods immediately following each blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Practical execution should be scheduled in the four weeks after each results announcement, which effectively narrows the collar entry and roll calendar to two short windows a year.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An express substantive ground for refusal: a senior executive hedging a large stake is exactly the transaction likely to fail a reputational perception test, independently of technical compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy extends to Connected Persons of Designated Persons in relation to dealing in AGL Securities ... (which will be read as if references to 'Designated Person' throughout the Policy was a reference to Connected Persons).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares or the borrowing through a family trust, controlled company or SMSF does not escape the secured financing ban or the approval requirement.

summary: A funded collar is not possible at AGL. The derivative legs themselves are workable in principle: paragraph 3.6 expressly permits Derivatives over AGL Securities that have vested and are not subject to a holding lock, and paragraph 4.2 confirms that a Designated Person may seek approval for a dealing in Derivatives over fully vested AGL Shares, with written approval from the Chair, CEO or Company Secretary according to the 4.2 matrix, valid for one week, outside the 1 July and 1 January blackout periods and any confidential Board blackout, and subject to the Front Page Test. The financing leg is fatal: paragraph 3.7 prohibits every AGL Employee from entering into margin loans or other secured financing arrangements in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as security against repayment, with no approval, hardship or grandfathering route, and the exceptional circumstances power in 5.1 extends only to disposals during blackout periods. Stock lending and short selling are also banned outright, and no Derivative may be used over unvested or holding-locked securities. Even an unfunded collar must clear the 3 month holding rule, which expressly catches arrangements that could result in disposal within 3 months of acquisition.
